comparison: Both evaluate the heterodimer characterization work (C52-C87, C148) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the convergent evidence from multiple analytical techniques, while peer reviewers explicitly praised the 'array of complementary techniques' and noted contamination was 'ruled unlikely.' Strong agreement on the quality and rigor of the characterization.

Both address cleavage and catalytic tyrosine mutation experiments. OpenEval (R3) covers C54-C55, C88-C93, C102-C105 as SUPPORTED. Peer (R2) covers overlapping claims C54-C55, C88-C106, C149-C150 as SUPPORTED. Both agree these provide key evidence for interface swapping mechanism, with peer reviewers noting contamination was 'ruled unlikely.'

OpenEval R4 addresses interface swapping mechanism (C56, C94-C101, C106-C107) as SUPPORTED. Peer R2 includes some overlapping claims (C94-C99, C102-C106) as part of broader evaluation. Both support the interface swapping interpretation, though peer review groups these with additional catalytic evidence.

Both evaluate kinetic cleavage assay data (C135-C138) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval R5 also includes C9-C10, C146 and emphasizes the delay demonstrating interface swapping kinetics. Peer R7 accepts these kinetic findings as supporting the mechanism, noting 'time lag consistent with rapid DNA-dependent subunit or interface exchange.'

Peer R3 addresses C9-C10, C56-C57, C107, C146 as SUPPORTED, providing 'convincing evidence for subunit swapping.' OpenEval R5 covers C9-C10, C135-C138, C146. Both support the core interface swapping finding, though they group different sets of supporting claims.

Both evaluate GyrB concentration effects (C58, C108-C118) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes that higher GyrB/heterodimer ratios stimulate double-strand cleavage, supporting GyrB's role in promoting interface swapping. Peer reviewers accepted these findings as part of comprehensive evidence showing factors facilitating subunit exchange.

Perfect claim overlap (C13, C119-C126) evaluating CTD deletion effects as SUPPORTED. Both agree the data show wrapping domain favors interface swapping. Peer reviewers noted 'Subunit exchange was facilitated by DNA bending and wrapping' as part of comprehensive evidence.

Perfect claim overlap (C11-C12, C60-C63, C127-C134) evaluating I174G mutant data as SUPPORTED. Both agree DNA bending favors interface swapping. Peer reviewers accepted these findings with praise for 'extensive and solid biochemical experiments, together with thorough experimental controls.'

OpenEval R9 addresses GyrB multimerization and higher-order complexes (C59, C69-C70, C72, C199, C234-C235) as SUPPORTED. Peer R1 includes some overlapping claims (C69-C70, C72) as part of broader characterization work. Both support the observation of multimeric complexes.

OpenEval R9 includes C234-C235 about GyrB multimerization as SUPPORTED. Peer R14 covers C234-C240 as SUPPORTED, accepting observations about multimeric complexes and dense packing. Both support these observations, though peer review extends to additional claims about DNA organization.

High claim overlap (C15, C64, C147, C196-C205) on mechanistic model. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the model is speculative and not directly tested. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting it as 'reasonable explanation' that 'opens new insights,' though acknowledging it's based on in vitro data. Subtle difference in confidence level.

Both address rapid vs. slow exchange distinction. OpenEval R11 covers C16-C17, C141, C143-C145, C221, C227 as SUPPORTED. Peer R8 covers broader set C16-C17, C139-C145, C221-C228 as SUPPORTED. Both agree on the distinction between rapid interface swapping and slow subunit exchange, with peer reviewers praising the comprehensive experimental controls.

OpenEval R12 addresses slow subunit exchange (C139-C140, C142, C222-C228) as SUPPORTED. Peer R8 includes overlapping claims (C139-C145, C221-C228) as SUPPORTED. Both agree these experiments demonstrate mechanistically distinct exchange processes with different properties and time scales.

Both evaluate arguments against swiveling mechanism (C151-C167 in OpenEval, C19-C20, C151-C188 in peer). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on theoretical arguments and experimental data. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED, stating the work 'provides further support for the accepted double strand break mechanism' and 'against a recently-proposed alternative mechanism.'

Both address reconciliation with Gubaev et al. work (C168-C188). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting reinterpretation involves speculation about contamination not directly tested. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the interpretation that addresses 'a puzzling paradox' with conclusions 'mostly well supported by the experimental data.' Difference in confidence about reinterpretation.

Perfect claim overlap (C189-C195) on fusion construct comparisons. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes data clearly show activity differences and interpretation is reasonable, though speculation about GyrB flexibility remains speculative. Peer reviewers accepted these comparative measurements as supporting data without challenge.

Perfect claim overlap (C18, C65, C217-C220, C229-C233, C241-C244) on in vivo implications and illegitimate recombination. Both rate as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes the model is speculative and not directly tested in vivo. Peer reviewers similarly note 'speculative nature of the in vivo implications' and state 'conclusions could be strengthened by in vivo data.' Strong agreement on uncertainty.

Both address gyrase packing on DNA (C236-C240). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on cleavage assays at high gyrase/DNA ratios, though notes in vivo organization inference is somewhat speculative. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting observations as part of comprehensive characterization without challenging the interpretation.

Both evaluate mechanistic interpretation of DNA binding/bending effects (C207-C216 in OpenEval, C100-C101, C211-C216 in peer). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes interpretation is reasonable and well-supported by I174G and BALLL.A data. Peer reviewers accepted as part of 'extensive and solid biochemical experiments' with appropriate controls.

OpenEval R1 evaluates background/foundational claims (C1-C6, C21-C30, C40-C42) about DNA gyrase structure and function as SUPPORTED, representing established knowledge. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers focused on novel experimental findings rather than background material.
